NEW DELHI: BJP on Monday announced eight candidates for the upcoming Rajya Sabha polls in Uttar Pradesh, leaving Union ministers Hardeep Puri and BL Verma out of the list.The party's Central Election Committee approved the names for the 2026 Rajya Sabha biennial elections in the state andThe announcement was issued by Tarun Chugh, Rajya Sabha MP and the BJP's national headquarters in-charge.The Election Commission of India (ECI) had earlier announced the schedule for biennial elections to 11 Rajya Sabha seats, 10 from Uttar Pradesh and one from Uttarakhand, which will fall vacant in November following the retirement of sitting members.The retiring members from Uttar Pradesh include Union minister Hardeep Puri, Arun Singh, Brijlal, BL Verma, Ram Gopal Yadav, Neerja Shekhar, Geeta alias Chandraprabha, Ramji, Seema and Dinesh Sharma. Naresh Bansal is the lone retiring member from Uttarakhand.Meanwhile, the Samajwadi Party has named Professor Ramgopal Yadav and Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani as its two candidates for the Rajya Sabha from Uttar Pradesh.The last date for filing nominations is October 6, followed by scrutiny of nomination papers on October 7. Candidates can withdraw their nominations until October 9. Polling will be held on October 16 from 9am to 4pm, with counting scheduled on the same day.
Article Summary: The party's Central Election Committee approved the names for the 2026 Rajya Sabha biennial elections in the state. Polling will be held on October 16 from 9am to 4pm, with counting scheduled on the same day. The retiring members from Uttar Pradesh include Union minister Hardeep Puri.

Article Title: 'Form 6 has not been approved by us': What SC said on EC's SIR decision - top quotes
Article Text:
What the top court said

Justice Suryakant said that any modification of Form 6 - the application citizens use to register as new electors - had not been approved by the top court. “Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let's be clear. When record is produced, we would like to see who has modified. But, your prayers appear jumbled up,” the CJI said.

The top court said that the transaction of business within the poll panel “has to be unanimous” and if it finds that certain decisions were taken by CEC without the required unanimity, it could reconsider or recall those decisions. “They are expected to take unanimous decisions. If there is no unanimity, it has to be by majority. If records show some decision was not unanimous, etc., we will injunct those decisions and say they are ultra vires. Can we ex parte come to a decision that all decisions were unilateral? We expect them to respond in a clear, transparent manner.”

“Let's first have authenticated information on that. We can always annul any decision,” the bench added.

“We presume that decisions are taken by Election Commission as per law,” the court said.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday declined to pass order on plea seeking suspend chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations that he took decisions on the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls without the consensus of the two other election commissioners.A bench led by CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also issued notice to the Centre, Election Commission of India and its three commissioners on a plea that alleged that the powers vested in the poll panel as a multi-member constitutional body were being exercised without following the collective decision-making mechanism mandated by law.The bench also rejected the poll body's claim that the top court had upheld the declaration attached to Form 6, making it clear that it had not approved any modification to the form.A report by the Indian Express claimed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders related to the SIR, alleging that some were issued without their knowledge or recommendation.The report said the poll panel's software added a requirement for ancestral details and a link to the previous SIR in Form 6, the voter registration form, without the legal amendment required under election rules.The poll panel however rejected the charges and said changes in the form were upheld by the Supreme Court . For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used," it had said.The poll panel had also said that differences of opinion are normal in institutional deliberations and maintained that all its orders are legally valid and follow the prescribed procedures.

Article Title: SC seeks EC response on changes during SIR: Why has Form 6 become a flashpoint — explained
Article Text:

The dispute over Form 6

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday raised questions over changes made to Form 6, the application used for registering a voter, during the Election Commission 's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The issue came up while the court was hearing petitions alleging that several decisions linked to the SIR exercise were taken without the approval of all three election commissioners, particularly Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, who were at odds with poll body chief Gyanesh Kumar on multiple occasions.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana sought responses from the Election Commission, the Centre, the CEC and the other two election commissioners before examining whether the poll panel's statutory procedure was followed.The bench, however, refused to pass an immediate order seeking the suspension of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, while considering the controversy over Form 6, which was one of the central issues raised in the petitions.Form 6 is the application through which an eligible person seeks inclusion of their name in the electoral roll. The Election Commission's guidelines states the application is addressed to the Electoral Registration Officer of the constituency where the applicant ordinarily resides.The form requires basic details such as the applicant's name, details of a relative, Aadhaar information, gender, date of birth and present ordinary residence. Applicants are also required to complete a declaration, with the guidelines warning that making a false statement in it is punishable under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.The Election Commission's instructions also mandates that an applicant can fill the form either in English or in the official language of the state. Also, an applicant who does not know the number or name of the relevant constituency cannot have the application rejected merely for that reason.For age verification, applicants can submit a self-attested copy of one of the documents specified in the form. The guidelines also provide for verification by the Electoral Registration Officer in cases where the prescribed documents are unavailable.The petitions allege that additional requirements connected with the SIR were introduced into Form 6 through the Election Commission's software.One of the allegations is that details concerning an applicant's ancestry (details of father or grandfather) and a link to the previous SIR were incorporated into the process without an amendment to the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.The petitioners have further alleged that Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi objected to the modification and that Election Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu subsequently endorsed the objection. Therefore, the issue therefore goes beyond the information sought from voters.At the heart of the dispute is whether the Election Commission could alter the form and introduce SIR-linked requirements through its software without following the legal process required for changing the relevant electoral rules. During the hearing, the CJI specifically flagged the question of who authorised the modification.“Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let's be clear. When record has produced, we would like to see who has modified. But, your prayers appear jumbled up,” the CJI noted, as quoted by LiveLaw.The court, however, did not accept the petitioners' allegations as established facts at this stage as Justice Bagchi said the court would first need responses from the concerned authorities and records before deciding whether any decision was taken contrary to the statutory framework."If records show some decision was not unanimous etc., we will injunct those decisions and say they are ultra-vires. Can we ex-parte come to decision that all decisions were unilateral? We expect them to respond in a clear, transparent manner," Justice Bagchi added.Amid the raging controvery, the Election Commission withdrew the additional SIR-related declaration from Form 6 in states where the electoral roll revision exercise had been completed.In states where the SIR was concluded, the EC removed additional declaration from the ECINET app and portal, as well as the respective Chief Electoral Officer portals. This meant that applicants in states where SIR is over will only need to fill the regular statutory Form 6 to enrol as voters.Just days before this action and as the controvery over dissent in the poll body emerged, the EC in a press note had, however, said that "the declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon’ble Supreme Court. For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used."The Form 6 dispute forms part of a broader challenge to how the Election Commission has allegedly handled the SIR exercise. The petitions rely on claims that the two other Election Commissioners formally raised objections on at least 14 occasions over several months to decisions and orders concerning the revision of electoral rolls.The allegations include changes to electoral-roll software, communications issued in the name of the Election Commission and other decisions allegedly taken without the approval of all members of the multi-member poll panel.The petitioners have invoked Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023. The provision states that the Commission's business should, as far as possible, be transacted unanimously and that where the members differ, the matter is to be decided according to the majority view.The pleas argue that this framework means powers vested in the Election Commission cannot be exercised individually by the CEC where the law requires the Commission to act collectively.The petitioners have sought several forms of relief, including suspension of Gyanesh Kumar as CEC until the matter is decided, preservation of electoral-roll data and audit trails, and restrictions on further substantive changes to Form 6.Another plea has sought criminal proceedings against the CEC and other officials and argued that decisions, guidelines and software changes allegedly made without the full Commission's agreement should be declared unconstitutional, ultra vires and void ab initio.The Supreme Court has therefore, at this stage, not ruled on whether the alleged changes to Form 6 or other SIR-related decisions were unlawful. The immediate question before the court is whether the Election Commission followed the statutory decision-making process.The court will consider the records and responses of the respondents before deciding whether any particular decision can be struck down.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Monday raised questions over changes made to Form 6, the application used for registering a voter, during the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The issue came up while the court was hearing petitions alleging that several decisions linked to the SIR were taken without the approval of all three election commissioners.

Article Title: Mamata 2021 injury row: Ex-CM's lawyer sends notice to hospitals over medical record 'disclosure'

NEW DELHI: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee 's lawyer on Monday sent a legal notice to state-run SSKM Hospital and the Bangur Institute of Neurosciences over the alleged disclosure of her medical records from 2021 without the Trinamool Congress (TMC) supremo's permission, PTI reported.The development came two days after West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari alleged at a press conference in Kolkata that Mamata Banerjee had "faked" her leg injury during the 2021 state assembly elections, which the TMC eventually won.Adhikari, a former Trinamool leader who joined the BJP in December 2020, displayed a document that he claimed was the March 11, 2021, report of the Bangur Institute of Neurosciences' Department of Radio Diagnosis. He said the report showed "no evidence of a fracture."Adhikari also announced that the state government would launch a fresh inquiry into what he described as Banerjee's "false claims" about her leg injury during the 2021 assembly election campaign.Following this, Mamata Banerjee's lawyer, Arka Nag, sent the notice to the director and medical superintendent of SSKM Hospital and the head of the neurology department at the Bangur Institute of Neurosciences.He sought an explanation as to how his client's medical records reached Adhikari and were subsequently made public. A copy of the notice was also sent to the principal secretary of the state health department.The notice referred to statements made by the chief minister on October 3 and argued that even if the medical records had been obtained by the state government or an investigating agency through a lawful process, that did not by itself authorise their disclosure to the public.It also sought to know whether the reports were disclosed pursuant to any court order and, if not, what action had been taken against those who provided the documents. The notice further sought clarification on whether the reports made public were the original medical records.The issue dates back to the 2021 West Bengal assembly election, when Mamata Banerjee, then chief minister and the TMC candidate from Nandigram, sustained injuries near Birulia Bazar while campaigning.She subsequently campaigned from a wheelchair, and the nature and extent of her injuries became a major political issue during the election.After the TMC returned to power, Mamata Banerjee, who at the time secure a third successive term as chief minister, was seen walking.
Article Summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari alleged that Mamata Banerjee had "faked" her leg injury during the 2021 state assembly elections. The issue dates back to the 2021 West Bengal assembly election, when MamataBanerjee sustained injuries near Birulia Bazar while campaigning.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Swiss Confederation president Guy Parmelin held wide-ranging talks in New Delhi on Monday, with the two sides discussing ways to deepen cooperation in trade and investment, mobility, infrastructure, defence, nuclear energy and critical technologies.The talks came as India and Switzerland seek to build on the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA), which entered into force last October and is set to complete a year of implementation this week.Addressing a joint press statement after the talks, PM Modi said the relationship between India and Switzerland had gained fresh momentum and highlighted the two countries' cooperation in innovation, infrastructure and advanced technology.“India-Switzerland friendship is centuries-old... Innovation, infrastructure and advanced technology are strong pillars of our foundation today. With the Summit today, we are going to give a new pace and height to our partnership,” PM Modi said.PM Modi said TEPA was an ambitious blueprint for investment, innovation, jobs and shared prosperity and set out a target of attracting $100 billion in investment into India and creating 1 million direct jobs over the next 15 years.“I am very happy to welcome the president of Switzerland to India. First of all, I would like to appreciate his commitment to India-Switzerland relations. With his personal support, last October we implemented a historic Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement between India and the European Free Trade Association, or EFTA, countries,” PM Modi said.“This is India's first FTA with any economic bloc in Europe,” he added.The Prime Minister said India and Switzerland had also taken decisions to increase market access for Indian exports to Switzerland and facilitate investment between the two countries.He said the measures would support exports of Indian agricultural products, pharmaceuticals, textiles and engineering goods, while encouraging Swiss investment in sectors including biotechnology, life sciences, banking, insurance, food processing and sustainability.The talks also expanded beyond trade and investment, with PM Modi saying the two countries had identified new opportunities for military exchanges and defence production cooperation.“We also agreed to further deepen nuclear energy cooperation,” he said.PM Modi pointed to projects such as the Varanasi ropeway, Noida's Jewar airport and railway and tunnelling projects in mountainous regions as examples of India-Switzerland infrastructure cooperation.The two sides also signed an agreement covering transport, mobility and infrastructure, with PM Modi inviting Swiss infrastructure companies to increase investment in India and participate in capacity-building, design and manufacturing.People-to-people ties were another focus of the discussions. PM Modi said the Migration and Mobility Partnership Agreement and Young Professionals Agreement signed during the visit would create new opportunities in Switzerland for Indian students, researchers, professionals and young people.Parmelin, who is on a three-day State visit to India, described the trip as an opportunity to further strengthen the long-standing relationship between the two countries.He said India and Switzerland shared democratic values as well as trust and mutual respect, and described his visit as a “stepping stone” towards deepening their partnership.The Swiss president's visit is also significant for TEPA, which was signed in March 2024 after nearly 16 years of negotiations and came into force in October 2025. The EFTA countries — Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway — have committed to investing $100 billion in India over 15 years under the agreement.Parmelin is scheduled to attend the second India-EFTA Prosperity Summit on October 7, marking the first anniversary of TEPA's implementation.Parmelin arrived in New Delhi earlier on Monday and was accorded a ceremonial reception at Rashtrapati Bhavan before visiting Rajghat to pay tribute to Mahatma Gandhi. He was accompanied by a delegation of senior officials and business representatives.External affairs minister S Jaishankar also met Parmelin and said he appreciated the Swiss president's commitment to deepening the India-Switzerland partnership and building on the promise of TEPA.According to the ministry of external aaffairs, Switzerland is India's largest trade and investment partner among the four EFTA countries.More than 330 Swiss companies currently operate in India across sectors including engineering, services, precision instruments, chemicals and pharmaceuticals, while Indian companies in Switzerland have a presence in areas including IT, pharmaceuticals and machinery.Parmelin will also meet President Droupadi Murmu, who is scheduled to host a banquet in his honour. The visit is his first State visit to India and his second trip to the country this year, after his participation in the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi in February.
Article Summary: Swiss Confederation president Guy Parmelin is on a three-day State visit to India. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Parmelin held wide-ranging talks in New Delhi on Monday. The two sides discussed ways to deepen cooperation in trade and investment, mobility, infrastructure, defence, nuclear energy and critical technologies.

Article Title: ‘Silence any woman who dares to ask questions’: Rahul slams Delhi Police over sexual harassment complaints
Article Text:

What Delhi Police said about the protest

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Monday accused the Delhi Police of mistreating women protesters and journalists during recent demonstrations in the national capital, after three women who identified themselves as journalists complained of alleged manhandling and sexual harassment by police personnel.In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi alleged that women were being silenced when they raised questions and demanded that CCTV footage from Saket police station be made public. He also sought action against police personnel accused of misconduct."What’s happening in Delhi right now follows a single pattern: silence any woman who dares to ask questions.Hundreds of people were detained at Jantar Mantar. Female protesters alleged that male police officers misbehaved with them. Cameras were snatched from female journalists, and they were dragged around. Not even an FIR was filed on a journalist’s complaint.A few weeks ago, Shaheen and Nafisa recounted their experiences of violence and mistreatment inside the Saket police station. Think about it—inside the station, the very place where women go to file complaints.Those entrusted with the responsibility of protecting women are now the ones posing a threat to them.And everyone in this country knows who the Delhi Police answers to.The entire CCTV footage from the Saket police station should be made public. Immediate action must be taken against the guilty police officers. Shaheen, Nafisa, and all those who have faced violence and rudeness from the Delhi Police must get justice.Mr Amit Shah—why are you and your police so afraid of women?"The Delhi Police, meanwhile, said three women journalists had submitted complaints alleging that they were manhandled by police officers and staff during their detention at a protest on October 3 against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Deputy commissioner of police Neha Yadav said the complaints had been registered, medical examinations conducted and the matter referred to the Crime Branch.“Around 6 PM, three women, who identified themselves as journalists, lodged a complaint alleging manhandling by Delhi Police officers and staff during their detention."“We request anyone possessing relevant footage to share it with the Crime Branch,” Yadav said.Delhi Police also confirmed that it had received complaints alleging sexual harassment by police personnel during the October 3 protest.“On 03-10-26, during the protest in New Delhi area, while being in law and order situation, allegations of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists against police officers. New Delhi District has received their complaints,” the police said in a post on X.According to police, protesters had been asked to vacate the site after Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita was imposed in the area. The protesters allegedly refused to comply and were subsequently detained.“Despite the imposition of Section 163 of the BNSS in the area, AISA and other parties staged a protest on October 3rd against the SIR. Protesters were warned to vacate the site, citing Section 163 of the BNSS; upon their refusal to comply, they were detained,” Yadav said.Several members of the All India Students' Association were detained by Delhi Police during the protest near Jantar Mantar. The demonstration was held against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as protests over the SIR exercise continued in the capital.Several protesters, including AISA president Neha Bora and senior advocates Prashant Bhushan and Kapil Sibal, attempted to cross police barricades near Jantar Mantar, according to the police account.Delhi Police has registered at least three FIRs in connection with the mass protest held near Jantar Mantar on October 2. Two FIRs were registered at Parliament Street police station and one at Connaught Place police station.
Article Summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi accused the Delhi Police of mistreating women protesters and journalists. Three women journalists complained of alleged manhandling and sexual harassment by police personnel. Delhi Police said three women journalists had submitted complaints alleging that they were manhandled by police officers and staff during their detention.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Swiss Confederation president Guy Parmelin at Hyderabad House in New Delhi on Monday as the Swiss leader began a three-day State visit to India aimed at strengthening bilateral cooperation.Parmelin's visit comes as India and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) prepare to mark the first anniversary of the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA), which entered into force on October 1, 2025.External affairs minister S Jaishankar also met the Swiss president. Sharing details of the meeting on X, Jaishankar said he appreciated Parmelin's sentiments towards deepening the India-Switzerland partnership and building on the promise of the India-EFTA TEPA.“Confident that his meeting with PM Narendra Modi will further our engagement across a wide range of domains,” Jaishankar said.Parmelin began his official itinerary with a ceremonial reception at Rashtrapati Bhavan, where he was received by President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Modi.Speaking to the media after the welcome ceremony, Parmelin described his visit as an opportunity to underline the importance both countries attach to their relationship.“The visit is an excellent opportunity to emphasise the importance that both Switzerland and India attach to this relationship,” he said.He said India-Switzerland ties were based on “shared democratic values as well as on trust and mutual respect”.“My visit is a stepping stone towards further growth, deepening and strengthening of our close, broad and long-standing partnership,” Parmelin said.He also highlighted the significance of the first anniversary of TEPA's implementation, saying it was a moment to assess the progress made by the two sides while looking towards future cooperation.“It is the right moment to celebrate how far we have come together, but even more importantly, to shape our joint future,” he said.During his three-day visit, Parmelin is expected to hold discussions with Indian leaders on trade, investment, science and technology, innovation, mobility, cultural exchanges and people-to-people ties. Regional and global issues, as well as multilateral cooperation, are also expected to feature in the talks.The Swiss president is travelling with a delegation of senior officials and business representatives. It is his first State visit to India and his second visit to the country this year after he attended the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi in February.Parmelin will also meet President Murmu, who is scheduled to host a ceremonial banquet in his honour.He is scheduled to attend the second India-EFTA Prosperity Summit on October 7, marking the first anniversary of TEPA's operationalisation.The EFTA comprises Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland. Among the four EFTA countries, Switzerland is India's largest trade and investment partner, according to the Ministry of External Affairs.“India and Switzerland share longstanding friendly relations. This visit will further strengthen bilateral relations, building upon the regular high-level exchanges and deepen cooperation in new areas of mutual interest,” the MEA said.
Article Summary: Parmelin's visit comes as India and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) prepare to mark the first anniversary of the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement. Parmelin is expected to hold discussions with Indian leaders on trade, investment, science and technology, innovation, mobility, cultural exchanges and people-to-people ties.

NEW DELHI: India produced another strong medal haul at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash. However, the impressive collection did not bring any change in the overall standings, with India remaining 12th as the country continued to wait for another gold medal.India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.'The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh, while Rohit Yadav, Parul Chaudhary, Vithya Ramraj and Pincky Balhara won bronze.India's strongest showing came in the men's javelin, where Yashvir and Rohit produced a double podium finish in the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra.Yashvir recorded a personal best of 85.72m for silver, while Rohit won bronze with 84.35m. Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: ‘Gyanesh must quit right away': Opposition backs Justice Bhuyan’s 'SIR strikes at Constitution's heart' remark
Article Text:
Opposition backs Supreme Court of India Judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan

'No amount of whataboutery can justify'

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh and Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra backed Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan after his remarks on voting rights and the disenfranchisement of citizens at an event in Hyderabad.Sharing a video of Bhuyan’s speech in an X post, Ramesh targeted chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and said that Bhuyan had “exposed the CEC lock, stock and barrel”.He also called on Kumar to quit, alleging that his ability to execute what he described as “G2’s illegal orders” had made him “a liability for the country”.TMC MP Mahua Moitra also praised the judge, saying it was rare for a sitting judge to “speak truth to power”. “Kudos to Justice Bhuyan,” she said.Speaking at NALSAR University of Law on Sunday, Bhuyan said the right to vote is integral to the basic structure of the Constitution. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution,” he said.Bhuyan further said the Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens, those with voting rights and those without them — and that wholesale disenfranchisement would violate Articles 14 and 326. He also said the right to vote or be included in the voters' list cannot be detached from a citizen’s status, comparing it to “taking out the soul from the body”.His remarks came amid the ongoing political and legal controversy over the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Article Title: Second Vande Bharat sleeper set to launch this month between Bengaluru and Mumbai; cutting travel time from 24 hours to under 16 hours, 30 year wait for faster connectivity between two cities to end
Article Text:
For more than 30 years, passengers have been seeking faster rail connectivity between Bengaluru and Mumbai.

Mumbai-Bengaluru Vande Bharat Sleeper: Expected Travel Time

What makes Vande Bharat sleeper special?

Vande Bharat sleeper: Indian Railways is all set to roll out the second Vande Bharat sleeper train after launching the first pair between Guwahati and Howrah earlier this year.After prolonged delays, the Railway Board is expected to issue the notification for the KSR Bengaluru-Mumbai CSMT Vande Bharat Sleeper shortly. According to sources, the train is likely to be flagged off later this month.The country's second Vande Bharat sleeper service is expected to substantially reduce the time taken to travel by rail between Bengaluru, India's technology hub, and Mumbai, its financial capital.Also Read | With better than Rajdhani experience & 160 kmph speed, can Vande Bharat sleeper trains be a game-changer for Indian Railways? Under the proposed schedule, the premium train will run six days a week in each direction, covering the distance in under 16 hours. At present, the Udyan Express, the only direct daily train connecting the two cities, takes an average of 24 hours to complete the journey.As per the tentative timings, the service may leave KSR Bengaluru at 10 PM and arrive at Mumbai CSMT at 1:50 PM the next day. On the return journey, it could start from Mumbai at 10:30 PM, reaching Bengaluru at 1:50 PM the following day. These are tentative timings and are subject to change.Although the official launch date has not yet been declared, the railway zones have been asked to commence the service at the earliest convenient opportunity.Its scheduled halts will include Anantapur, Guntakal, Raichur, Kalaburagi, Solapur and Kalyan, according to this TOI report For more than 30 years, passengers have been seeking faster rail connectivity between Bengaluru and Mumbai. Despite repeated assurances, train journeys between the two cities continue to take considerable time.The proposed Vande Bharat Sleeper service is expected to address this long-standing demand and improve connectivity between the cities.The Vande Bharat sleeper train has 16 passenger coaches. The rake includes 11 AC 3-tier coaches, four AC 2-tier coaches and one AC First Class coach.The train has been designed to operate at speeds of up to 160 kmph, while its testing speed is 180 kmph, placing it in the semi-high-speed category. However, most sections of the Indian Railways network are not equipped to permit trains to operate at such high speeds.Drawing on design elements seen in European trains, the Vande Bharat sleeper coaches feature cushioned berths aimed at providing greater comfort. The design of the upper berths has also been modified to make climbing up easier for passengers.Passenger amenities include dedicated night lights, integrated public announcement systems accompanied by visual displays, CCTV cameras and modular pantry units.The sleeper train is also equipped with modern bio-vacuum toilets similar to those used in aircraft. A separate toilet designed for disabled passengers also has a baby care station. Passengers travelling in AC First Class additionally have access to shower facilities with hot water.For safety, the Vande Bharat sleeper train comes fitted with the indigenous KAVACH anti-collision system. Like the chair car versions of Vande Bharat, the sleeper variant will also use regenerative braking technology to improve energy efficiency.Automatic interconnecting doors have been provided between the coaches. The gangways are fully sealed, helping maintain clean air inside the train as well as effective temperature control.Passenger convenience features in every coach include individual reading lights, charging points and refreshment tables. The interiors use GFRP panels. The train doors are designed to open automatically at designated stations.The train also comes with a Centralised Coach Monitoring System. An emergency communication facility allows passengers to communicate directly with the driver when required.Meanwhile, ICF is also working on developing its own version of the Vande Bharat sleeper train.
Article Summary: The KSR Bengaluru-Mumbai CSMT Vande Bharat Sleeper is likely to be flagged off later this month. The premium train will run six days a week in each direction, covering the distance in under 16 hours. At present, the Udyan Express, the only direct daily train connecting the two cities, takes an average of 24 hours.

Article Title: 1 dead as Russian drones hit desi pharma plant in Ukraine

Six Russian drones struck an Indian pharma plant in Ukraine’s Sumy Sunday in what Kusum Group cofounder Sanjeev Gupta described as a “targeted attack”, killing an engineer and injuring some others. The main structure of the facility was largely destroyed.Speaking to TOI, Gupta said the attack was not an isolated incident and claimed that pharmaceutical and food facilities in Ukraine had also come under attack over the past month. “Six drones hit the factory. So, it is a targeted attack. It’s not by chance. Actually, for the last one month, they are attacking all pharma and food items also,” Gupta said.The plant was operational when the strikes took place, Gupta said. The engineering department was hit and one engineer was killed, while other workers were evacuated.Gupta said the extent of damage could keep the plant out of operation for at least one to two years.“We are not able to evaluate the losses right now. We will come to know more tomorrow. But as per my understanding, we will not run this plant in the near future,” he added.In a statement issued later Sunday, Kusum Healthcare Pvt Ltd said total damage from the attack was projected to breach the $50 million mark.The company said its India business and management were reviewing the situation as the extent of the destruction emerged. The Sumy facility covers around 50,000 sq metres and has five blocks, Gupta said.It has been manufacturing medicines in Ukraine since 2009, including products for segments such as cardiology and gastroenterology. Gupta said Kusum is the biggest Indian pharmaceutical company operating in Ukraine, with a market share of more than 3%. The latest attack is not the first major strike on Kusum’s Ukrainian operations.The company said its warehouse was destroyed by a Russian drone on April 14, 2025, with losses from that attack exceeding UAH 1 billion.Despite the latest setback, Gupta said the group plans to continue its business in Ukraine.

Article Title: External affairs minister S Jaishankar says US has chosen to become 'lonelier power'
Article Text:
External affairs minister S Jaishankar addresses the 62nd Munich Security Conference in New Delhi

World today is marked by America’s radical repositioning and China’s rise, says Jaishankar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Foreign minister S Jaishankar said US had deliberately chosen to become a "lonelier power", while reiterating Russia's longstanding support for India."At a time when much of the world preferred backing a military regime next to us (Pakistan), Russia was a country with which our relations were very good, and we are shaped in many ways by that legacy," he said at Munich Leaders Meeting here.He said India's Russia-Ukraine conflict approach had moved beyond just the advocacy of dialogue, suggesting India might now be looking to actively mediate.Both Moscow and Kyiv have said recently that India had come up with ideas and proposals to bring an end to the war. Unlike China and others that have looked to mediate, India had so far supported global peace efforts — advocating dialogue between the parties — but had not come up its own proposal, reflecting its emphasis on bilateral resolution of disputes.Offering a teaser on India’s proposal, Jaishankar said India is looking to address some immediate concerns that both Russia and Ukraine have on “grain exports, energy exports, non-attack possibilities”.“We would like to see an end to this conflict. This will require dialogue and diplomacy. We have been advocating it for many years, and in recent months we have got a little bit more involved beyond advocacy. We have conversations with both Russia and Ukraine in this regard.We are trying to be helpful, starting with the Black Sea safety of shipping issue,” said the minister, speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting here.Jaishankar had said during his visit to Ukraine last month — shortly after PM Narendra Modi’s message to Russian President Vladimir Putin to stop the “endless war” — that India was discussing ideas that could be developed for cessation of hostilities.On Friday, while Putin announced Modi had very good ideas for peace, Ukraine’s foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said India had come up with the “broadest” peace proposal out of the four that it had received from other countries, including the US.This shift in India’s position seems driven by direct domestic fallout of the conflict, whether it’s commercial shipping disruptions in Black Sea or an intense blowback from US over India’s continued purchase of Russian crude.On US, Jaishankar said the world today was marked by a radical repositioning of the US, and also the rise of China.“The current system was significantly underwritten by the United States. That underwriting is diluting.” He underlined that the sharp competition between US and China was not limited to them alone. “It has led to weaponisation of any leverage that any country has. ”
Article Summary: S Jaishankar said US had deliberately chosen to become a "lonelier power", while reiterating Russia's longstanding support for India. He said India's Russia- Ukraine conflict approach had moved beyond just the advocacy of dialogue, suggesting India might now be looking to actively mediate.

Article Title: 'Want to see who modified Form 6': SC refuses to pass interim order to suspend CEC Gyanesh Kumar
Article Text:
SC on Monday heard two pleas against CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

What did the petitioners seek?

What is the EC SIR row?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to pass an interim order seeking the suspension of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and issued notice to the Election Commission of India, CEC and the other two election commissioners on a plea challenging decisions taken by the poll body on Special Intensive Revision.A bench led by CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana heard pleas filed by Patna resident Rakesh Kumar Singh and advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi. The pleas raised questions over whether Gyanesh used powers belonging to the Election Commission without the approval of election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.“Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let's be clear. When record has produced, we would like to see who has modified. But, your prayers appear jumbled up,” the CJI noted.The apex court directed the respondents to file their responses to the allegations. The court said it would examine whether the statutory scheme was followed and indicated that if the records showed that any decision was not taken in accordance with the law, it could injunct such a decision and hold it ultra vires."If records show some decision was not unanimous etc., we will injunct those decisions and say they are ultra-vires.Can we ex-parte come to decision that all decisions were unilateral? We expect them to respond in a clear, transparent manner," Justice Bagchi added.One of the plea sought Gyanesh's suspension until the final hearing to protect the “multi-member character of the Election Commission”. It asked that Sandhu and Joshi run the commission's business together in the meantime and that any vacancy be filled on the recommendation of a committee that includes the Chief Justice of India.However, the second plea sought criminal proceedings against the CEC and other officials for allegedly failing in their official duty. It further sought a declaration that all decisions, guidelines and software changes made under Gyanesh without the full commission's agreement are “unconstitutional, ultra vires and void ab initio”, meaning illegal and invalid from the start.Tripathi's plea relies on Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, which says the majority view prevails when commissioners differ. The plea argued that the law requires decisions to be taken together.A report by the Indian Express claimed that commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders relating to the SIR, which were allegedly issued without their knowledge or recommendation.On Form 6, the voter registration form, the plea alleges that a requirement for ancestral details and a link to the previous SIR was added through the poll panel's software without the legal amendment the election rules require. It claims the other two commissioners objected to the change.On Goa, it alleges that the software lacked a feature to restore 97 eligible voters despite directions to verify them.On West Bengal, it claims more than 16.10 lakh appeals were filed in the EC's name against voters whose names were restored by judicial officers. It says the other two commissioners and the state's chief electoral officer did not know about these appeals or approve them.The Election Commission has said differing views are a normal part of discussions in any institution and that all its orders are legally valid and follow the set procedures.
Article Summary: Supreme Court on Monday refused to pass an interim order seeking the suspension of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. A bench led by CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana heard pleas filed by Patna resident Rakesh Kumar Singh and advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi. The pleas raised questions over whether CEC used powers belonging to the Election Commission without approval.

I feel enormously proud and privileged that I am now in a party which has undertaken welfare works for people in West Bengal in the past few months.”The bypolls for 12 Rajya Sabha seats across West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand are scheduled for October 16.

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan
Article Text:

Detaching right to vote from citizen is like taking soul out of body: Bhuyan

NEW DELHI: Launching a scathing attack on special intensive revision (SIR) that has resulted in large-scale deletion of names from voter lists across states, Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution.Discounting the reasons given by govt and EC to justify SIR, which was upheld in the case of the revision of rolls in West Bengal by SC with modifications, Justice Bhuyan said, "No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of Constitution. I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution."He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad.Nalsar students, who had opposed CJI Surya Kant's participation in the convocation ceremony recently, came in for praise from Justice Bhuyan.Also read| Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman "One last word about the brilliant students of Nalsar. You have shown to the country and to the world what a university student, that too a student of law, should be. You are brilliant, you are bold, and you are brave," he said.Justice Bhuyan said a citizen’s right to vote was central to the holding of free and fair elections.“Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing,” he added.The SC judge said the right to vote or be included in the voters’ list could not be detached from the persona of an Indian citizen.Also read: EC orders special drive to add genuine electors 'left out' during SIR “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added. Justice Bhuyan said the Indian Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens: citizens with voting rights and citizens without voting rights. “Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution of India,” he said.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary,” he added, his remarks coinciding with attacks on EC and govt over SIR by the opposition and others.Justice Bhuyan said the right to vote was intertwined with India’s years of struggle against foreign rule. “It is a manifestation of our freedom achieved after so much struggle and sacrifice. Article 326 (universal adult franchise) cannot be tinkered with at all. No authority can do it, no court can condone it. No one is above Constitution,” he said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution. He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad. “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added.

Article Title: No room to roam: The cost of a crowded planet for wild animals
Article Text:
What shrinking habitats do to India's wildlife

A shrinking home, not a vanishing one

Not just about wildlife, it’s about the essential ecosystems that sustain human life

What changes for an animal that loses space

Elephants outside the fence

The country holds about 60 per cent of the world's Asian elephants

Tigers on islands of forest

Where Kaziranga ends

The state wants to replace the default 10-km eco-sensitive zone (ESZ) around Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve

Wetlands and the quieter losses

The cost to people

Where space is being rebuilt

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What the evidence points to

Animals do not simply move on when their habitat shrinks. Their numbers thin out

Over the past fifty years, the average size of monitored wildlife populations around the world has fallen by 73 per cent, according to WWF's Living Planet Report 2024. The report names loss and degradation of habitat as the most commonly reported threat, driven mainly by how the world grows its food.This finding raises a plain question. When animals lose the land, water and forest they depend on, what happens to them?Habitat rarely disappears all at once. It is cut into pieces by farms, roads, canals, railway lines, power lines and growing towns. Each piece may still have trees and water, but it supports fewer animals than the original whole did.The 73 per cent figure also needs careful reading. It describes the average change across thousands of monitored populations. It does not mean that three-quarters of the world's animals are gone, or that three-quarters of species have disappeared. What it does show is a steady thinning, and the report describes such declines as an early warning of greater risk to species and ecosystems. The pressure it describes is gradual and widespread rather than the result of a single event, which is partly why it is easy to overlook. The report also notes that some populations have held steady or recovered where conservation has worked.“This is not just about wildlife, it’s about the essential ecosystems that sustain human life,” said Daudi Sumba, chief conservation officer at WWF.The effects usually arrive in a recognisable order. Food and water become harder to find, so animals travel farther to reach them. Their routes cross fields, highways and railway tracks. Animals with large ranges, such as elephants and big cats, are affected first, because they need the most room.Smaller populations face a slower problem. When forest patches are cut off from one another, animals cannot move between them to find mates. Over time a small, isolated group becomes more vulnerable to disease and to sudden shocks such as drought or fire. Wherever forest meets farmland or settlement, animals and people also meet more often, and not always safely.India's elephants show how this plays out. The country holds about 60 per cent of the world's Asian elephants, according to the last census in 2017. Most of them do not live inside protected areas. Government and press figures put the share outside reserves at about 80 per cent. That share matters for everything that follows. A herd that lives mostly outside reserves has no boundary between it and the land that people farm, travel across and build on.For these herds, a journey between feeding grounds can pass through paddy fields, village lanes, rail lines and overhead power cables. Official data tabled in Parliament in 2024 shows what that means. Over five years, the leading cause of unnatural elephant deaths was electrocution, ahead of train accidents, poaching and poisoning. Odisha, Assam, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu reported the largest numbers of electrocution deaths.The government has taken some steps in response. It has identified and ground-validated about 150 elephant corridors, the routes herds use to move between forests. The Railways and Environment ministries have also formed a standing committee to reduce deaths on tracks.Tigers tell a more hopeful story, with a warning attached. The 2022 estimate counted at least 3,682 tigers in India, a record, spread across 53 tiger reserves. These reserves are among the best protected forests in the country.But the same assessment shows the limits of protection. Roughly a third of the reserves need stronger protection, habitat restoration or more prey for the tigers to feed on. A few reserves in Mizoram, Nagaland and Jharkhand reported almost no tigers at all. Summaries of the report also describe many reserves as small islands of forest, joined to one another by a limited number of corridors. A reserve with a healthy tiger population can send young animals out in search of territory of their own, and many of them end up in unprotected land among farms and villages.The record count and the weak reserves belong in the same account. Protection works where it is applied well, and the gaps appear where it is not.Kaziranga's protection does not stop at the park boundary, and a new proposal from the Assam government has put that line under debate. The state wants to replace the default 10-km eco-sensitive zone (ESZ) around Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve with a site-specific zone of one to three kilometres. An ESZ is a regulatory buffer, declared by the environment ministry on a state's proposal. It is not an outright ban: depending on the notification, activities in it may be prohibited, regulated or permitted, and mining is among those most strictly restricted.Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma says the 10-km limit applies only because Kaziranga has not yet been finally notified. He argues it brings populated areas such as Kaliabor, Doboka and Jakhalabandha under restrictions, and holds up civic projects like a proposed stadium in Bokakhat. The state says the park's boundary and its UNESCO World Heritage status will not change, and that the 10-km zone stays in force until a new one is notified. Some residents agree. Hundreds rallied in support of the proposal on August 18, saying the current limits get in the way of building homes and basic infrastructure.The opposition and conservationists are not convinced. Congress state president Gaurav Gogoi led a protest at the Kohora range and alleged that the change could give legal cover to mining. The state government rejects the charge. Conservationists such as Jadav Payeng and Kavita Ashok point to the annual floods, when rhinos, deer and elephants move to higher ground outside the park. A smaller zone, they warn, could cut off those routes.A 2025 conservation assessment notes that a smaller zone is not necessarily a weaker one if it is designed to protect the most sensitive areas. Whether it does will depend on the final notification, which will decide whether wildlife corridors, flood escape routes and wetlands fall inside the line.Space does not only mean forest. Globally, freshwater species have seen the steepest declines in the WWF report, and wetlands are often among the first places to be drained or built over.The report points to Chennai, where rapid urban growth has led to a large loss of wetland area. Wetlands shelter birds, fish and amphibians, and they also soak up floodwater for the city around them. When they go, wildlife loses a home and people lose a buffer.When space runs out, people pay too. Government data tabled in Parliament showed that elephants killed 2,853 people in India over five years, with the highest toll in 2023. Many of these deaths happened in places where farms, villages and elephant routes overlap. The elephant deaths and the human deaths come from the same stretches of land, where both now depend on the same ground.The Environment Ministry has issued guidelines on managing human-elephant conflict, and it says compensation is provided for losses. These measures respond to the damage after it happens. They do not by themselves restore the space that animals have lost.Some efforts aim at the cause. West Bengal has begun a community programme called Gajamitra, or Friends of Elephants, in which local people take part in reducing conflict. Conservation scientists have also suggested low-cost methods for farmers, such as planting chillies, ginger or citrus around fields, which elephants tend to avoid, or placing beehives along field edges.The WWF report also records progress in India, where it says some wildlife populations have stabilised or recovered. It credits government initiatives, careful habitat management, scientific monitoring and community involvement. At the global level, the report calls for more effective conservation along with changes in food, energy and finance systems.The picture from India and from the world is consistent. Animals do not simply move on when their habitat shrinks. Their numbers thin out, they wander into danger, they come into conflict with people, or they disappear from places they once held. Where land is protected, connected and shared with the people who live beside it, some populations hold their ground or recover.India's own examples point in both directions: electrocutions and train deaths on one side, a record tiger count and recovering populations on the other. The difference lies largely in whether land is protected and linked together, and whether the people who live beside wildlife are part of the plan.The question on World Wildlife Day is how much room is left for wildlife, and who decides what happens to it.
Article Summary: India holds about 60 per cent of the world's Asian elephants. Government and press figures put the share outside reserves at about 80 per cent. A herd that lives mostly outside reserves has no boundary between it and the land that people farm, travel across and build on.

Former Maharashtra chief minister and senior Congress leader Prithviraj Chavan on Sunday rejected Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray ’s call to boycott elections, saying participation in elections was a democratic right.“I do not accept that we should boycott the election. Raj Thackeray called for the SIR exercise in Maharashtra to be scrapped and for elections to return to ballot papers.“Our demand is that the entire SIR conducted in Maharashtra should be cancelled,” Raj Thackeray said.“The law says that SIR is conducted if an emergency situation arises,” he said, questioning the circumstances in which the revision was undertaken.Raj Thackeray also alleged that 40 to 60 lakh voters were added during the Maharashtra Assembly elections and claimed that two crore voters were now being removed through SIR.“Forty to sixty lakh voters were added during the Assembly elections, and power was captured through this. Article Title: Government set to halt sugarcane juice, B-heavy molasses diversion for ethanol
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Government is set to disallow diversion of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses for ethanol production in the 2026-27 ethanol supply year (ESY) starting November, amid an around 11% shortfall in sugar production from initial estimates for the 2025-26 sugar season and indications of a further decline in output due to drought in major sugarcane-growing states of Maharashtra and Karnataka.TOI has learnt that government will notify the decision soon, ahead of the start of the new ESY. While ethanol supply year runs from Nov 1 to Oct 31, sugar season in India runs from Oct 1 to Sep 30. Government specifies the quantity of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses that can be diverted for ethanol production to meet the mandatory blending target for the green fuel in petrol.The move comes at a time when domestic sugar supplies remain tight. Mills diverted about 30 lakh tonnes of sugar, or around 10% of total output, for ethanol production during the sugar season that ended on September 30. The new sugar season began on October 1 with opening stocks of around 37.5 lakh tonnes, compared with nearly 50 lakh tonnes a year ago.Industry sources said there was no scope for allowing further diversion of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses for ethanol, as ensuring adequate domestic sugar supplies remains a priority for both govt and mills.With the possibility of a fall in output in the current season, particularly in Maharashtra and Karnataka, government would prioritise sugar availability over additional diversion for ethanol.Disallowing the use of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses for ethanol in 2026-27 would enable mills to produce more sugar from the available cane, helping augment domestic supplies and meeting consumption requirements.Government has said that the share of sugar diverted for ethanol has declined from around 12% in 2022-23 to around 9% in 2025-26. Besides, nearly three-fourths of ethanol produced in the country now comes from grains, particularly maize, reducing the dependence on sugar-based feedstock.“Meeting the demand for 20% ethanol blending in petrol won’t be an issue. With indications of millers getting a better price, it won’t be a problem for them either. Government would have to continue with the ban on exports and may have to allow more imports as well,” an industry analyst said.Sugar production in the 2025-26 season was hit by crop diseases, waterlogging and adverse weather in key producing states. Against the initial production estimate of around 343 lakh tonnes, output was estimated at around 306 lakh tonnes in August, including the quantity diverted for ethanol production.After accounting for the diversion to ethanol, net sugar production in 2025-26 was around 279 lakh tonnes, barely enough to meet the normative domestic consumption requirement of 280-285 lakh tonnes.
Article Summary: Government is set to disallow diversion of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses for ethanol production in the 2026-27 ethanol supply year (ESY) The move comes amid an around 11% shortfall in sugar production from initial estimates for the 2025-26 sugar season. Mills diverted about 30 lakh tonnes of sugar, or around 10% of total output, for ethanol during the sugar season that ended on September 30.

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Sunday said the global landscape was being shaped by a “radical repositioning” of the United States and the rise of China, while asserting that India has the potential to move rapidly up the global power hierarchy in the coming years.Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, Jaishankar said the US had “deliberately become a lonelier power” as part of a chosen change in its posture.“No one in the room would disagree with the fact that the landscape today is primarily marked by a radical repositioning of the United States. A repositioning which is a posture of choice and, in a way, it has deliberately become a lonelier power,” Jaishankar said.He identified the rise of China as the second major feature of the changing global order, pointing to the increasingly sharp competition between the two powers.“That competition today, not limited to these two countries, has led to a weaponization of any leverage that any country has. And that competition coexists with the complexity of interdependence,” he said.On India’s prospects, Jaishankar said the country had “decades of high growth” ahead and a demographic profile capable of supporting that growth.He also said India may not have to follow the traditional industrialisation path taken by earlier economies.“I would even argue, a world that is much more creative, where many new possibilities are there, so that we don't necessarily have to tread the earlier path of industrialization,” he said.“The orthodox path will have to devise something much more contemporary for what awaits us,” he added.Jaishankar said countries currently classified as middle powers could follow different trajectories as the global order evolves.“Among the middle powers, some will peel off, some will stay put, some may drop down a bit,” he said.“That is the reality. That will be part of the evolution of the global order,” Jaishankar added.The Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi is being held on October 4 and 5, bringing together senior decision-makers and experts to discuss international security and foreign policy issues.
Article Summary: External affairs minister S Jaishankar said the global landscape was being shaped by a “radical repositioning” of the United States. He said the US had “deliberately become a lonelier power” as part of a chosen change in its posture. He identified the rise of China as the second major feature of the changing global order.

Hyderabad turned into a global meeting point for the real estate sector as the 7th International Real Estate Conference (IREC 2026) brought together more than 2,000 delegates from over 35 countries at HITEX from September 25 to 27.The three-day conference, hosted by the Hyderabad Realtors Association (HRA) with the National Association of REALTORS®–India (NAR-India) as a strategic partner, brought developers, institutional investors, realtors, policymakers, technology leaders and property professionals onto a common platform.The event brought together the Global Conference, IREC Luxury Property Expo and Innovation Showcase, with discussions spanning institutional investment, changing buyer behaviour, branded residences, holiday homes, affordable housing, real estate tokenisation, cross-border transactions and the growing role of PropTech, artificial intelligence, data and DeepTech.One of the key highlights of the conference was the launch of the India Housing Report – September 2026, prepared by NAR and CRE Matrix. Based on H1 2026 data, the report put the value of primary housing sales across India's Tier-I cities at ₹3.63 lakh crore, broadly unchanged from the record level recorded in H1 2025.According to the report, 2.58 lakh housing units were sold during the first half of 2026, a decline of around 2% year-on-year, while new launches rose about 7% to 2.98 lakh units.The Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) remained the largest housing market, accounting for around 26% of pan-India housing value, followed by NCR at 19%. MMR recorded approximately ₹93,800 crore in primary housing sales.Navi Mumbai and Raigad recorded 29% growth in housing value, with volumes rising around 20%, while Bengaluru recorded 25% growth in housing value and accounted for approximately 17% of the national housing value.IREC 2026 featured participation and perspectives from markets including the US, Dubai, Philippines, Georgia, Canada, Japan, Mongolia, China, Korea, Taiwan, Cambodia, Indonesia and Vietnam.The discussions focused on strengthening India's integration with global real estate markets, attracting institutional and international investment, facilitating cross-border transactions and exploring the creation of a more connected global real estate marketplace.The conference was inaugurated by Majid Saqer Al Marri, Real Estate Registration & Services, Dubai Land Department, while Kevin Brown, President, National Association of REALTORS® (NAR), inaugurated the IREC Luxury Property Expo.For Hyderabad, the conference provided a platform to examine the city's real estate growth against the backdrop of international investment, urbanisation and technology-led transformation.Speaking at the inauguration, Sumanth Reddy, Chairman, NAR-India, said the real estate sector was changing faster than the traditional transaction cycle, with increasingly informed buyers, more global capital flows and technology reshaping the way business is conducted.Mr. D.Sridhar Reddy, Founder & Past President - HRA and NAR-INDIA, said hosting IREC in Hyderabad was aimed at placing the city in a wider global real estate conversation and ensuring that discussions remained practical and relevant to professionals across markets.Shailender Singh, Chairman, IREC 2026, said changing buyer preferences, cross-border investment and emerging technologies were creating new opportunities as well as new questions for the industry.The conference also featured sessions on Dubai's real estate model, institutional investment, India's growth opportunities, affordable housing, tokenisation, branded residences, urban development and the future of PropTech and DeepTech, alongside the Luxury Property Expo and Innovation Showcase.
Article Summary: The 7th International Real Estate Conference (IREC 2026) brought together more than 2,000 delegates from over 35 countries at HITEX from September 25 to 27. NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Monday dismissed a batch of petitions seeking an SIT probe into the 2020 Delhi riotsand the violence at Jamia Millia Islamia during anti-CAA protests in December 2019.A bench of Justices Vivek Chaudhary and Manoj Jain said, “for the reasons mentioned in the judgment, all the petitions are dismissed”.“The batch is decided into two parts, one is northeast Delhi riots and another is for Jamia Millia riots,” the bench said while pronouncing the verdict, PTI reported.The court also rejected pleas seeking registration of FIRs against political leaders over alleged “hate speeches” linked to the 2020 riots and action against police officers accused of dereliction of duty. You can't have an EC which functions or malfunctions like this. So the first important red flag qua the Constitution and the common man is the appointment process of election commissioners. Article Title: 'Look Out Circular' against parents of man who secretly took away child to US
